extractor.note: Partial pass over the section that states the method, plus the section on the pure ego-attitude.

coverage_note: Covers 'The Method of Phenomenological Reduction. Transcendental Phenomenology as A Priori Science of Pure Consciousness' and 'The Pure Ego-Attitude and the Idea of a Transcendental Phenomenology' in Part I. The remaining sections of Part I and all of Part II are not covered.

units.claim: The first and most important piece of the reduction is the phenomenological epoché suspending the totality of outer realities, hence the whole universe.
units.quote: The first and most important piece of this reduction is the suspension, the phenomenological epoché regarding the totality of outer realities, hence of the whole universe.

units.claim: The reduction has two components: suspension of all position-taking on the existence of external realities, and the recognition that the being of consciousness survives that suspension.
units.quote: It has two components: (1) the epoché — the suspension of all position-taking regarding the existence of external realities; and (2) the recognition that this suspension leaves the being of consciousness itself intact.

units.claim: The reduction is not a repetition of Cartesian doubt: indubitability is a characteristic of the domain it discloses rather than the aim of the procedure.
units.quote: The phenomenological reduction is not a repetition of Cartesian doubt but an essentially new methodological achievement.

units.claim: The bracketing harbours no skepticism about objective existences and relinquishes no conviction about the world; it is a methodological principle of abstaining from judging about the objective.
units.quote: the bracketing of all objective existences, does not harbor any skepticism regarding them or indeed a devaluation of what we call "objective existence."

units.claim: The world is not simply excluded by the reduction but rediscovered within consciousness as its intentional correlate, which opens constitutional phenomenology as a field.
units.quote: the world is not simply excluded by the reduction but rediscovered within consciousness as its intentional correlate

units.claim: What remains after the comprehensive reduction is transcendental phenomenology as an a priori science of the essential structures of pure consciousness.
units.quote: What remains after this comprehensive reduction is transcendental phenomenology: an a priori science of the essential structures of pure consciousness.

units.claim: A theoretical reduction is described as the exclusion of all theoretical and other opinions gained through justifying thinking, leaving what is found in perceptual givennesses.
units.quote: in theoretical reduction, i.e., under exclusion of all theoretical and in general all opinions gained through justifying thinking
